t-bar-reverse-row.why: A heavy row for your lats.
setup: Chest on the pad, feet flat.
Start with your arms straight.
form: Pull your shoulders back first, then pull your elbows toward your hips.
Hold 1 second at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.
tips: Elbows close to your body work the lats more. Elbows out wide work the upper back more.
avoid: Lifting your chest off the pad.
Shrugging up instead of pulling back.

single-arm-cable-lat-pulldown.why: Stretches and works your lats, one arm at a time.
setup: Pulley up high. Kneel or sit facing it.
Hold one handle with your arm straight up.
form: Pull your elbow down to your side.
Let your arm go back up slowly until you feel the stretch.
tips: Pull with your elbow, not your hand.
Pause 1 second at the top.
avoid: Stopping before your arm is fully up.

single-arm-db-row.why: Works the lower part of your lats.
setup: One hand and knee on a bench, back flat.
Dumbbell hangs straight below your shoulder.
form: Pull your elbow back toward your hip.
Lower until your arm is straight and your shoulder blade spreads forward.
tips: Pull toward your hip, not your chest.
avoid: Turning your body to lift more.

straight-arm-cable-pulldown.why: Works your lats without your biceps helping.
setup: Pulley up high, bar or rope.
Step back and lean forward a little.
form: Keep your arms almost straight.
Pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze.
Let your arms go back up slowly.
tips: A rope lets your hands go a bit past your hips.

db-incline-curl.why: Your arms hang behind you, which stretches the biceps.
setup: Bench tilted back to 45–60°, lie on it.
Arms hanging straight down, palms forward.
form: Curl up without moving your elbows forward.
Lower all the way until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders on the bench.
avoid: Stopping before your arms are straight.

barbell-preacher-curl.why: Works the biceps hardest near the bottom.
setup: Armpits at the top of the pad, upper arms flat on it.
An EZ bar is fine if a straight bar hurts your wrists.
form: Curl up and stop just before your forearms point straight up.
Lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
avoid: Dropping fast at the bottom. It's hard on the elbows.
Lifting your elbows off the pad.

machine-shoulder-press.why: Works the front of your shoulders and your triceps.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at chin height.
Back flat on the pad.
tips: Don't arch your back off the pad.

cable-lateral-raise.why: Works the side of your shoulders the whole way up and down.
setup: Pulley low, one arm, cable in front of your body.
Hold the machine with your free hand and lean away.
form: Start with your hand across in front of your body to stretch the shoulder.
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height, elbow leading.
Lower slowly, all the way back across.

lateral-shrug-hybrid.why: A heavy trap exercise: a small side raise and a shrug in one move.
setup: Heavy dumbbells at your sides.
Use straps if your grip gives out first.
form: Lift your arms out a little while shrugging your shoulders up to your ears.
Hold 1 second, then lower slowly.
tips: Shoulders to ears is what matters. Arm height doesn't.

barbell-shrug.why: Heavy work for your upper traps.
setup: Bar in front of you, hands just outside your thighs.
Stand tall.
form: Shrug straight up and hold 1 second.
Lower all the way down.
tips: Use straps so your grip doesn't give out first.

overhead-trap.why: Works your lower traps, which work hardest with your arm overhead.
form: Raise your arm in a big arc until it's over your head.
Finish in a Y, slightly in front of your head, thumb up.
Hold 1 second at the top, lower slowly.
tips: At the top, reach up as high as you can.
Go light enough to reach the top every rep.

machine-reverse-fly.why: Works the back of your shoulders.
form: Open your arms back wide until they line up with your body.
Bring them back slowly.
tips: Don't squeeze your shoulder blades together hard.

smith-squat.why: A heavy squat for your quads.
setup: Bar across your upper back.
Feet shoulder width, under or a little in front of the bar.
form: Sit down until your thighs are level with the floor, no deeper.
Stand up, pushing through the middle of your feet.
tips: Feet more under the bar works the quads more.
avoid: Going below level. It works the glutes more.

setup: Back of your knees at the edge of the seat, knees lined up with the machine's pivot.
Pad just above your ankles.
form: Straighten your legs and squeeze 1 second.
Lower slowly.
tips: Leaning back a little gives the quads a bigger stretch.
avoid: Kicking the weight up and letting it drop.
Lifting your hips off the seat.

prone-leg-curl.why: Works your hamstrings with the knees fully bent.
setup: Lie face down, knees just past the edge of the pad.
Pad just above your heels.
form: Curl your heels up toward your butt.
Lower slowly until your legs are almost straight.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the pad.

setup: Sit tall, pads on the inside of your knees.
Start as wide as you can control.
form: Squeeze your legs together and hold 1 second.
Open slowly back to the stretch.
Lower your heels as far as you can and pause 1 second.
Rise up as high as you can.

wide-grip-lat-pulldown.why: A heavy pulldown for your back.
form: Pull the bar to your upper chest.
Let it go back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Let your shoulders rise at the top to feel the stretch.

cable-seated-row.why: A heavy row for your back.
form: Row to your lower ribs and squeeze 1 second.
Let your arms go straight and your shoulder blades spread.
tips: Leaning forward a little at the stretch is fine. Swinging back isn't.
avoid: Using your lower back to throw the weight.

setup: Lie on a bench tilted back to 30–45°.
Arms straight up, tilted slightly back.
form: Bend only your elbows and lower the bar behind your head.
Straighten your arms back up.
tips: Keep your upper arms still. Only your forearms move.

machine-dip.why: A heavy press for your triceps.
setup: Sit up straight.
form: Push down until your arms are straight.
Let the handles come back up as far as is comfortable.
tips: Sitting upright keeps the work on your triceps.

v-bar-pushdown.why: Works your triceps with your arms at your sides.
setup: Pulley up high, V-bar.
Elbows at your sides, lean forward a little.
form: Push down until your arms are straight and squeeze.
Let your forearms come up just past level.
tips: The squeeze with straight arms is the point.

rope-face-pull.why: Works the back of your shoulders and upper back. Good for shoulder health.
form: Pull toward your forehead and pull the rope apart.
Finish with your hands beside your ears, elbows high.
tips: Go light and controlled.

lean-away-lateral-raise.why: Leaning away gives a longer range of motion, so your side delts work from a deeper stretch.
setup: Pulley low. Hold the machine with one hand and lean away, about 15–30°.
Cable handle in the other hand.
form: Raise your arm to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.

all-the-way-up-lateral-raise.why: Side of your shoulders up to shoulder height, then traps above it.
setup: Light dumbbells.
form: Raise your arms out to the sides, past shoulder height, almost overhead.
Lower slowly.
tips: Use lighter weights than a normal side raise.
avoid: Swinging to get the weight up.

setup: Chest on the pad of a row machine.
Arms straight, holding the handles.
form: Squeeze your shoulder blades together without bending your elbows.
Hold 1 second, then let them go forward.
tips: It's a short move. Make the squeeze count.

single-arm-cable-reverse-fly.why: Works the back of your shoulder with a cable.
setup: Pulley at shoulder height.
Hold the handle with the far hand, across your body.
form: Swing your arm out and back at shoulder height, elbow slightly bent.
Bring it back across slowly.
tips: Keep your shoulder down and your body still.

rope-overhead-tricep-extension.why: Stretches and works your triceps overhead.
tips: Keep your elbows pointing forward and still.

db-hammer-curl.why: A heavy curl with palms facing in. Builds thicker arms.
setup: Palms facing each other, elbows at your sides.
form: Curl one arm at a time up to your shoulder.
Lower all the way.
tips: Add weight once you get 10 clean reps on every set.

leg-press.why: A heavy press for your quads.
setup: Feet low on the platform, shoulder width.
form: Lower until your knees are bent about 90°.
Push back up without locking your knees hard.
tips: Feet lower on the platform works the quads more.
avoid: Going so deep your lower back rounds.

seated-leg-curl.why: Works your hamstrings with a big stretch.
setup: Lap pad tight, knees lined up with the machine's hinge.
form: Curl your legs all the way.
Straighten them slowly.
tips: Leaning forward gives a bigger stretch.

form: Lower your heels all the way and pause.
Rise up as high as you can.
tips: Pause at the bottom every rep.

cable-one-arm-tricep-kickback.why: Works your triceps with the arm fully straight.
setup: Pulley low, one handle, lean forward.
Upper arm at your side, level with the floor.
form: Straighten your arm and squeeze 1 second.
Bend it back to about 90°.
